newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt reselling some Brazilian raw contracts.
newsitem.headline: Egypt reselling some Brazilian raw contracts.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company and private Egyptian sugar importers have agreed to resell some of their Brazilian raw sugar contracts because of a surplus, traders said on Tuesday.
Representatives of the two sides met in Cairo on Saturday and came to the conclusion that the market could not take all the sugar which they have contracted to import, they said.
"The contracts must be renegotiated and resold. These are contracts under joint accounts between the sugar company and the traders," one trader said.

Egyptian companies have contracted for about 500,000 tonnes of raws but there is already so much white sugar on the market that the sugar company cannot even sell the sugar it has refined from domestic production, they said.
The domestic price of white sugar has fallen to 1,420 pounds ($418) a tonne from 1,600 pounds, they said.
The traders said they expected to make a profit from the resale of the contracts because the world price has risen. The sugar company and the traders will share the gain.
In the case of some other contracts, delivery will be deferred to March 1998 from July 1997, they added.
